name: The Bound Branches
meaning: Two charcoal branches bound with ochre carry checked dependencies between workers.
prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this inherited square prehistoric cave wall. Preserve exact size 1254x1254, framing, warm rock, cracks, illumination and ALL existing marks exactly in place: central heavy-lidded wide-mouth Pepe frog, his five-digit hands, basket, colored paths, upper balance, upper-right four-way stones, right shelter, bottom-right basket. Add only one small earth-pigment mark on the bare left-upper rock around x=170..285 y=320..430: two rough charcoal branches joined by a tiny red-ochre woven binding, symbolizing checked dependency links. Flat worn thumb-and-burnt-stick pigment, rock showing through. Do not add hands, figures, writing, letters, numbers, logos, border, watermark. Never erase, move, redraw or clean existing marks. The rock is the inherited background; new pigment must look like prehistoric hand painting. Save the final PNG in the workspace at artifacts/gathering/wall-v7.png if supported; do not save any other image in workspace.
finishing: Node preservation pass selects generated branch/binding pigment; final patch [225,322,100,160]. No additional image saved in workspace.

visual_review.method: Worker inspected full final PNG and 512-pixel JPEG with view_image, compared inherited wall and preservation measurements.
visual_review.pepe: Inherited wide mouth and heavy-lidded eyes preserved.
visual_review.palette: charcoal black and red ochre, with original rock showing through

limitations: Inherited rock looks photographic; preserved as required, no photograph or render introduced by new pigment.
Very small knot and grain details diminish in the JPEG.
Structural checks and worker visual review are not independent artistic certification.
